newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada firms building Saskatchewan heavy oil line.
newsitem.headline: Canada firms building Saskatchewan heavy oil line.

text.p: The Canadian units of Mobil Corp and Murphy Oil Corp and Canada's CS Resources Ltd said on Thursday they started construction of a C$9.8 million heavy oil pipeline system in west-central Saskatchewan.
The system, which will carry about 38,000 barrels a day of heavy oil and condensate, was expected to be completed on December 1, the firms said.
The North-Sask Pipeline is a jointly owned, dual-line project that will extend to Murphy's Manito Pipeline at Dulwich, Saskatchewan from heavy oil fields north of the North Saskatchewan River.
the Manito pipeline will, in turn, deliver the blended heavy oil and consensate to the IPL Energy Inc system at Kerrobert, Sakatchewan.
The companies said the new line would joint Mobil's Celtic Pipeline with proposed tie-ins to the Murphy oil battery at North Tangleflags, Saskatchewan.
In 1997, another new pipeline connection is planned to CS's Paradise Hills heavy oil properties.
The companies said the new system, to be operated by Murphy, would consist of about 70 km of pipe ranging in diameter from three inches to 10 inches.
